mechanism_inventory: access-control mismatch (isValidMessageCall checks caller but interactorsByChainId can be set to zero/empty, allowing spoofed source)
missing invariant enforcement — setInteractorByChainId permits empty/zero bytes, disabling trusted-source check silently
wrong lifecycle ordering — interactorsByChainId entry can be overwritten or zeroed after deployment
unauthorized state deletion — owner can map any chainId to zero bytes
value exceeds bound — keccak256 comparison with ZERO_BYTES sentinel
precision/packing/normalization edge — keccak256 of empty bytes is ZERO_BYTES sentinel
external-call failure/DoS — _isValidCaller enforces msg.sender == connector; decommissioned connector bricks receipt

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: setInteractorByChainId accepts an arbitrary bytes value including empty bytes; owner can silently overwrite or zero-out a chain's trusted interactor at any time with no timelock or multi-sig, allowing owner-controlled bypass of cross-chain message authentication (register attacker address as trusted interactor).
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Compromised or malicious owner calls setInteractorByChainId(targetChainId, attacker_bytes), then sends a cross-chain message whose zetaTxSenderAddress matches the registered attacker address.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Owner calls setInteractorByChainId(sourceChainId, attackerAddressBytes). 2. Cross-chain message via connector with zetaTxSenderAddress==attackerAddressBytes. 3. isValidMessageCall passes. 4. onZetaMessage executes with attacker data.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Users/counterparty chains — funds/state gated behind onZetaMessage/onZetaRevert accessible to attacker.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker/malicious owner spoofs trusted cross-chain messages.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: setInteractorByChainId has no timelock/multisig/value-validation; single-EOA owner can overwrite the cross-chain trust registry. Different actor path (owner) and state (interactorsByChainId) than the connector-caller check.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: keccak256(new bytes(0)) is the ZERO_BYTES sentinel; setInteractorByChainId does not prevent registering empty bytes. For a chain with empty/unset interactor, a message claiming zetaTxSenderAddress==new bytes(0) passes isValidMessageCall (keccak256('')==keccak256('')), bypassing the trust registry for unregistered chains.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Attacker observes interactorsByChainId[chainId]==empty (never set or zeroed); crafts a cross-chain message with sourceChainId=that chain and zetaTxSenderAddress=new bytes(0).
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Chain X interactor unset/zeroed. 2. message via connector sourceChainId=X, zetaTxSenderAddress=empty. 3. keccak256(empty)==keccak256(interactor)==ZERO_BYTES — passes. 4. onZetaMessage executes attacker payload.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Any user whose funds/state are protected by cross-chain authentication on an unregistered/zeroed chain.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker injects arbitrary messages from unregistered chains.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Distinct from owner-overwrite: exploits the ZERO_BYTES sentinel collision in default/unset state; requires no privileged action (only connector cooperation, the standard delivery mechanism). Source: ZERO_BYTES = keccak256(new bytes(0)) and modifier comparison defaults to empty bytes.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: external-call failure / DoS — connector immutable; if ZetaConnector paused/decommissioned, inheriting contracts permanently lose receipt
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: connector public immutable; _isValidCaller enforces msg.sender == address(connector) with no fallback.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether ZetaConnector has a pause/decommission path — requires ZetaConnector source.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: All users of inheriting cross-chain contracts (liveness).

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: isValidRevertCall reverts if sourceChainId != currentChainId (immutable from block.chainid).
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Attacker must supply correct sourceChainId — intended constraint, not bypass.

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: revert must return to originating contract (address(this)); spoofing requires compromising connector.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Check enforced; only trusted connector could forge.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Ability to inject arbitrary cross-chain messages into inheriting contracts (fund transfers/state corruption depending on inheriting logic).
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Anonymity if zero-address path used (no privileged action).
impact_direction.victim_loses: Funds/state integrity protected by cross-chain message authentication.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Cross-chain source authentication: messages should only be accepted from registered trusted interactors on registered chains; ZERO_BYTES sentinel collision allows unregistered chains to bypass.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: zero-bytes bypass requires no admin privilege and no timing window — structural flaw in default/unset state for any unregistered chain.
